thread:
alex: Hey folks — seeing intermittent packet loss between pods on the dedicated-gpu pool in eu-west-3. Spikes started ~11:08 UTC, lots of gRPC retries from the checkpointer. Any ideas?

noah: Yup, same. GRPC retries + increased p99 latency for model-save calls. Snippet from checkpointer logs: 
```
2026-02-15T11:08:12Z checkpointer ERROR rpc failed: context deadline exceeded (retries=3)
2026-02-15T11:08:12Z checkpointer WARN retransmit detected: 12 pkts, rto=200ms
```

maria: I ran tcpdump on node-123 during a spike. Lots of retransmits followed by a burst of large segments that look like offloaded fragments. tcpdump -n summary: 
```
11:08:12.123 IP 10.10.5.2.42345 > 10.10.6.7.50051: Flags [P.], seq 123:245, ack 98, win 64240, length 122
11:08:12.124 IP 10.10.5.2.42345 > 10.10.6.7.50051: Flags [.], ack 220, win 64240, length 0 (Retransmission)
11:08:12.130 IP 10.10.5.2 > 10.10.6.7: UDP, length 1450  # vxlan inner bursts
11:08:12.131 IP 10.10.5.2 > 10.10.6.7: UDP, length 1450
```

alex: Interesting — we run vxlan with MTU ~1450 on vxlan iface, host eth0 is 1500. My hunch: a burst from checkpointing (big sequential writes) creates large skbs which get segmented/offloaded; VXLAN/GRO/GSO interaction plus MTU mismatch causes kernel to drop some fragments or offload mis-apply, leading to retransmits.

noah: Can you paste ip link and ethtool -k from the node? I pulled this from node-123: 
```
$ ip link show vxlan0
4: vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group 239.0.0.1
$ ip link show eth0
2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
ethtool -k eth0 shows GRO: on, GSO: on, TSO: on. mlx5 driver present.

maria: ethtool -k dump: GRO: on, rx-checksumming: on, tx-checksumming: on, gso_partial: on. Also saw "udp-frag-offload: on" on some hosts.

alex: I did a quick canary on node-123: disabled GRO/GSO/TSO with `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` before the next checkpoint. The retransmits dropped almost immediately for that node during the subsequent checkpoint run. CPU on that node went up ~8% for the checkpoint pod but tail latency for model-save improved.

noah: That's a useful signal. Disabling offloads will reduce performance for network-heavy workloads but seems to avoid the pathological path. We should be cautious fleet-wide — CPU cost vs. packet reliability tradeoff.

maria: There's a known interaction between mlx5 offloads + vxlan/geneve and kernel versions; our kernel is 6.2.12 on those dedicated nodes. CI notes a regression in vxlan offload handling in some 6.2.x series. Could consider driver/firmware upgrade (mlx-ofed) or kernel patch, but that'll take time.

alex: Immediate mitigation plan: roll a small canary in eu-west-3 dedicated pool (3 nodes) with GRO/GSO off. If stable, expand to rest of dedicated nodes in region. Long term: either fix driver/kernel or set vxlan mtu equal to eth0 and enable fragmentation-safe path (but that may require cluster-wide reconfigure).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: canary-group=dedicated-gpu-eu-west-3-3nodes job=canary-2026-02-15-12:30 id=cb-4521

noah: If canary works, let's implement node-init changes via a DaemonSet that runs ethtool flags on boot for dedicated nodes only. Also add autoscaler hook to annotate new nodes so the init runs.

maria: Also asking infra-research to capture a kprobe stack for when GSO -> vxlan path triggers a drop, and record whether RDMA fallback is happening for those NICs. If RDMA falls back under high load, that could explain bursts.

alex: I'll open an incident and tag eng-sre + eng-infra + eng-runtime. Incident INC-2026-117. Will post rollout results here and link postmortem. For now: canary at 12:30UTC, monitoring p50/p95/p99, cpu, and retransmit counters.

noah: Thanks — if anyone sees other regions, ping here. Also capture `ip -s link` and `ss -s` during spikes; that'll help correlate sockbuf drops.

maria: Adding checklist: 1) canary gro/gso off (in progress) 2) capture tcpdump + ethtool on affected nodes 3) kprobe for gso->vxlan 4) plan driver/kernel upgrade path 5) add node-init daemonset if mitigation held.

alex: Good. I'll post results in ~30m. :thumbsup:
